topic: Boundary-complete proxy-cycle target rigidity for selected probabilities of causation. In the exact finite Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki four-response-type model with binary treatment and outcome, finite proxies, latent confounding, outcome-dependent selection, positive observed selected tables, and nonnegative latent proxy mechanisms, define the full normalized response-cycle factorization fiber. Treat separately the two-proxy design with supplied positive population cell margins and the relevant-IV design with unknown margins and shared-Z equations. Prove an observable rank/support/cycle criterion that is necessary and sufficient for PN/PS constancy on every nonempty mixed-rank and boundary fiber. Emit rational formulas where possible and exact algebraic certificates otherwise; on every nonrigid stratum emit two legal full SCMs with identical observables and margins but different targets, requiring strict-positive twins only in interior strata. Prove termination and fixed-alphabet exact output bounds, stable Wald inference on separated rigid strata, and multinomial confidence-fiber inversion near rank/support transitions. Apply the atlas to the GEUVADIS SWAP70-to-SBF2-AS1 selected-expression analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the full nonnegative cycle-to-SCM lift, a complete all-rank-two orientation-box atlas including an identified assignment boundary, the stacked-rank-four affine-annihilation branch, and an exact relevant-IV residual-ratio/forest reduction with one cycle-product constraint. A complete mixed chart yields a cubic nuisance root and legal target-changing completions; fourteen mixed two-proxy and eight unknown-margin IV instances were checked exactly. Forced-zero boundaries, coincident lines, inactive rows, hidden Z splits, cross-face comparisons, and current NMF/counterfactual collisions were tested. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove explicit mixed-support cycle target elimination across every real component and support face, with target agreement tests or legal twin extraction, without reducing the classification to generic two-copy quantifier elimination. EARLY KILL TEST: Compile the residual-ratio/forest rules for ternary inactive-row and coincident-endpoint patterns and compare them with exact full-fiber elimination on independently sampled rational observable tables; any missed target-varying component kills the classifier, while an irrational singleton must use the authorized exact-algebraic branch. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_proxycycle_target_rigidity.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly, for every nonempty two-proxy fiber with supplied positive population cell margins, including rank-deficient and forced-zero mechanism faces, when PN and PS are constant by an observable rank/support/cycle criterion.

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies probabilities of causation under confounding and selection bias using two proxy covariates, but gives regular invertibility-based conditions rather than a necessary-and-sufficient boundary classification.
source_refs.author: Ryusei Shingaki, Haruka Yoshida, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: Two independent proxies identify a causal effect under a rank condition; when rank fails, the paper supplies a causal-null test rather than a complete target-rigidity atlas.
source_refs.author: Wang Miao, Zhi Geng, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Shingaki–Yoshida–Kuroki recovery argument relies on observable matrix inversions, so it no longer decides identification when ranks fall, proxy endpoints coincide, rows become inactive, or a latent mechanism reaches a nonnegative boundary. Miao–Geng–Tchetgen likewise separates the full-rank case from rank failure without asking whether PN or PS remains invariant despite nuisance nonuniqueness. Generic latent-class and NMF uniqueness results do not settle this question because a causal target can be rigid while the underlying factorization is not.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite semialgebraic disjunction in observable ranks, supports, and cycle products that is necessary and sufficient for PN/PS constancy, with a rational identifying formula or exact algebraic certificate on each rigid stratum and two legal observationally equivalent SCM completions with different targets on each nonrigid stratum.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest motivation arc, finite response-type model, two-proxy design, selection mechanism, and PN/PS definitions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PN/PS answer individual attribution questions -> confounding and outcome-dependent selection defeat classical formulas -> two proxies restore identification under regular invertibility -> determine exactly when the targets remain identified beyond invertibility and on boundary fibers

method_exemplars.technique: Use admissible-factorization tangent cones and rigidity matrices to characterize infinitesimal and local motions, followed by a separate global-component analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The normalized proxy model is an exact nonnegative factorization with extra cycle equations; target rigidity asks whether the PN/PS functional annihilates every legal motion and agrees across global components.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply data-based partial-identifiability conditions sequentially to recover only the factor columns required by a target rather than demanding full factor uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: PN/PS may be constant while latent proxy mechanisms remain nonunique, paralleling partial identifiability of selected NMF factors.

method_exemplars.technique: Use plug-in recovery for finite response-type probabilities and prove asymptotic normality from the regular local identifying equations despite the ambient singular model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates the same kind of four-response-type probabilities and provides a natural regular-stratum estimator once the atlas supplies a locally smooth identifying branch.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a boundary-complete necessary-and-sufficient PN/PS rigidity atlas for the relevant-IV-plus-proxy design when population margins are unknown and latent decompositions are coupled by shared-Z equations.

source_refs.claim: Its second design uses an instrumental variable and one proxy to identify PN and PS from selected data under stated positivity and matrix conditions, while unavailable population margins preclude analogous PNS recovery.
source_refs.author: Ryusei Shingaki, Haruka Yoshida, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: Instrument and covariate information identify response-type probabilities under regular moment conditions, but the paper gives no all-support classification of a shared-instrument fiber.
source_refs.author: Yuta Kawakami, Ryusei Shingaki, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: A causal linear functional may remain identified and root-n estimable when the proxy-bridge solution is nonunique, motivating target rather than nuisance uniqueness.
source_refs.author: Jeffrey Zhang, Wei Li, Wang Miao, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The regular IV derivation uses residual ratios and shared-instrument restrictions only where the relevant denominators and ranks are nonzero. Unknown margins introduce latent scaling directions, while shared-Z equations couple response cells, so neither cellwise inversion nor a standard IV rank condition determines PN/PS constancy. The nonunique-bridge literature establishes the analogous possibility of functional uniqueness, but its linear integral-equation argument does not handle nonnegative response cycles, inactive instrument rows, coincident endpoints, or disconnected support faces.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable residual-ratio/forest-and-cycle criterion equivalent to PN/PS constancy over the full unknown-margin shared-Z fiber, with exact formulas or algebraic-number certificates on rigid components and legal same-observable, different-target SCM pairs on every nonrigid component.

writing_exemplar.why: Its instrumental-variable design fixes the destination model and clearly exposes the information lost when population margins are absent.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selection and latent confounding obstruct attribution -> a relevant IV plus a proxy supplies linked observable equations -> regular inversion identifies PN/PS despite unknown margins -> classify precisely which degenerate shared-Z fibers preserve that information

method_exemplars.technique: Translate instrumental and covariate restrictions into moment equations for finite potential-outcome-type probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the nearest finite-response-type IV machinery; the new proof changes its regular inversion step into componentwise support and cycle elimination.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize legal local motions of a nonnegative factorization through rigidity matrices and polyhedral tangent constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Inactive rows and coincident endpoints create boundary motions that must be intersected with the shared-Z equations before target annihilation can be checked.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a nuisance solution set, select a canonical solution by extremum estimation, and debias the target functional to obtain root-n regular inference without nuisance uniqueness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The IV proxy fiber may be non-singleton while PN/PS is singleton-valued, matching the separation between functional identification and nuisance recovery.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct inference for PN/PS that is Wald-efficient on strata separated from rank/support discriminants yet remains uniformly coverage-valid along local sequences approaching rank loss, forced zeros, or transitions from point to set identification.

source_refs.claim: The proxy response-type estimation problem is singular, while the proposed plug-in estimators are asymptotically normal under regular identifying conditions.
source_refs.author: Ryusei Shingaki, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: The observational response-type estimator uses augmented-Lagrangian recovery and proves asymptotic normality while recognizing that standard likelihood methods fail for the singular model.
source_refs.author: Ryusei Shingaki, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: Counterfactual-bound inference becomes nonregular when latent response strata create optimization ambiguities; stabilized one-step inference is proposed for that setting.
source_refs.author: Johan de Aguas, Sebastian Krumscheid, Johan Pensar, Guido Biele

source_refs.claim: Conditional tests in moment models attain uniformly correct asymptotic size without assuming identification and remain efficient under strong identification.
source_refs.author: Isaiah Andrews, Anna Mikusheva

open_problems.why_unsolved: Delta-method variances require a fixed smooth identifying branch and nonsingular Jacobian, precisely what disappears near proxy-rank and support transitions. Stable inference for counterfactual-bound endpoints and identification-robust conditional tests address related nonregularities, but neither treats a multinomial observed table whose confidence region must be intersected with a changing semialgebraic SCM fiber and projected onto PN/PS. A pointwise switch between Wald and partial-identification intervals can therefore undercover along contiguous sequences approaching the discriminant.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A hybrid confidence procedure with a separation-index theorem yielding the regular Wald limit away from the discriminant and a multinomial confidence-fiber inversion theorem giving uniform asymptotic or finite-sample coverage for PN/PS across all local rank/support-transition sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from a counterfactual target to partial identification, optimization ambiguity, nonregular inference, and a stability remedy.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Cross-world benefit probabilities may be only partially identified -> endpoint optimization can have ties or latent null strata -> ordinary asymptotics become unstable -> build inference valid at ambiguity and identification transitions

method_exemplars.technique: Condition out the functional nuisance parameter in a Gaussian limit experiment and invert quasi-likelihood-ratio tests with size uniform over identification strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rank loss in the proxy equations creates weak-identification sequences; conditional test inversion can preserve coverage without selecting a vanishing-rank chart.

method_exemplars.technique: Stabilize one-step corrections with stratum-specific matrices when nonsmooth counterfactual-bound optimizers are ambiguous.
method_exemplars.why_closest: PN/PS switches between smooth point formulas and nonsmooth fiber extrema at atlas boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert exact e-variable tests for multinomial contingency-table functionals to obtain an observable-law confidence region before nonlinear projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Confidence-fiber inversion begins with multinomial selected-cell uncertainty and projects an exact or anytime-valid observable-law region through the SCM feasibility correspondence.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp attainable lower and upper bounds for PN and PS on every nonrigid two-proxy or relevant-IV selected-data fiber, including disconnected boundary components and unknown population margins.

source_refs.claim: Tian and Pearl derive theoretically sharp PN, PS, and PNS bounds from experimental and observational laws under minimal binary SCM assumptions, but without proxy mechanisms or outcome-dependent selection.
source_refs.author: Jin Tian, Judea Pearl
source_refs.venue: Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence

source_refs.claim: The paper derives nonparametric bounds for a causal risk difference under outcome-dependent sampling and unmeasured confounding, where the bounding problem need not reduce directly to linear constraints.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, Arvid Sjölander
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Proxy variables yield partial identification without completeness through nonsmooth bounds and bootstrap inference, but the targets are causal effects rather than selected cross-world PN/PS.
source_refs.author: AmirEmad Ghassami, Ilya Shpitser, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Tian–Pearl sharpness uses a response-type polytope with linear observable constraints, whereas selected proxy-cycle models impose bilinear nonnegative factorizations and cycle products. Gabriel–Sachs–Sjölander treat outcome-dependent sampling but target a marginal risk difference, and Ghassami–Shpitser–Tchetgen treat proxy-induced partial identification but not selected cross-world PN/PS or coupled response cells. Two target-changing completions certify nonidentification but do not determine whether intermediate values are attainable, whether disconnected real components have disjoint target images, or whether an endpoint is an irrational algebraic singleton.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Exact sharp endpoint formulas or algebraic certificates for the PN and PS images of every nonempty fiber, together with endpoint-attaining legal SCMs and a proof that the union over all real support components is complete.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames partial identification as the response to outcome-dependent selection and latent confounding and emphasizes nonlinear bounding constraints.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome-dependent sampling distorts population causal information -> latent confounding blocks point identification -> bounds retain what the design supports -> derive sharp PN/PS bounds under additional nonlinear proxy-cycle restrictions

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize PN/PS functionals over response-type probabilities and prove sharpness by constructing compatible SCM distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination targets are identical; the new proof replaces the response-type polytope with a semialgebraic selected proxy-cycle fiber while retaining constructive endpoint attainment.

method_exemplars.technique: Reparameterize outcome-dependent sampling restrictions and derive sharp causal bounds when the original problem is not directly a linear program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest selection-aware nonlinear bounding argument, although its target and proxy constraints differ.

method_exemplars.technique: Use stabilized one-step correction with stratum-specific stabilizing matrices for nonsmooth counterfactual-bound endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: PN/PS fiber endpoints are nonsmooth at support and component transitions, matching nonregularity induced by ambiguity in latent response-stratum optimization.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the GEUVADIS SWAP70-to-SBF2-AS1 analysis satisfies the proxy, instrument, selection, and margin correspondences required for PN/PS identification, and produce an atlas-stratum certificate or an observationally equivalent nonidentification pair when it does not.

source_refs.claim: The case study maps rs7124238, SWAP70 expression, SBF2-AS1 expression, coarse population labels, and an introduced selection variable into the IV-plus-proxy selected-data model; reported PN/PS estimates reach boundaries.
source_refs.author: Ryusei Shingaki, Haruka Yoshida, Manabu Kuroki

source_refs.claim: MRPC applies Mendelian-randomization constraints to GEUVADIS graphs but reports that some inferred topologies fail to replicate in GTEx, potentially because of weaker correlations and gene-specific measurement error.
source_refs.author: Md. Bahadur Badsha, Evan A. Martin, Audrey Qiuyan Fu

source_refs.claim: The GEUVADIS analysis treats genetic variants as natural instruments for orienting direct and indirect gene targets under Mendelian-randomization and confounding assumptions.
source_refs.author: Md. Bahadur Badsha, Audrey Qiuyan Fu

source_refs.claim: GEUVADIS generated population-stratified RNA-seq and genotype data from 465 lymphoblastoid cell lines, providing the observational substrate reused by the SWAP70/SBF2-AS1 case study.
source_refs.author: Tuuli Lappalainen et al.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The AISTATS case study treats coarse ancestry labels as a latent-confounding proxy and introduces selection for illustration, whereas the MRPC sources motivate causal orientation from Mendelian-randomization constraints and document cross-cohort instability and possible measurement error. These ingredients do not themselves verify proxy exclusion relations, the selection law, population-margin assumptions, or the response-type factorization. Boundary estimates make regular plug-in interpretation especially fragile, so the unresolved task is a correspondence-and-identification audit rather than another numerical application of the regular formula.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A formal data-to-SCM correspondence theorem and computable diagnostic placing the GEUVADIS table in a certified atlas stratum, followed by either a justified PN/PS formula with a transition-robust confidence set or two legal same-table SCMs proving nonidentification.

writing_exemplar.why: It is the exact destination application and specifies the variable mapping that must be audited.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gene-regulatory attribution is scientifically meaningful -> GEUVADIS supplies genotype, expression, and population structure -> proxy-plus-IV formulas produce PN/PS numbers under a selected SCM -> certify the assumptions and identification stratum before interpreting those numbers

method_exemplars.technique: Use Mendelian-randomization edge constraints with conditional-independence tests to distinguish direct from indirect gene targets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the biological IV correspondence and identifies which causal-direction assumptions the PN/PS model must reconcile.

method_exemplars.technique: Map the selected genotype/expression/proxy table into finite response-type factorization equations and recover PN/PS under regular rank conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed audit retains this exact model but replaces assumed regularity with an observable atlas certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct exact or anytime-valid confidence regions for contingency-table probabilities before nonlinear target projection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The GEUVADIS analysis begins with modest-size discretized cell counts, for which observable-law confidence inversion is safer than a boundary-sensitive bootstrap of a rational PN/PS formula.

literature_map:
Pearl (1999, Synthese, DOI 10.1023/A:1005233831499) defines PN, PS, and PNS and establishes their basic SCM identification logic.
Tian and Pearl (2000, Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence; arXiv:1301.3898) give sharp binary probabilities-of-causation bounds from observational and experimental laws.
Kuroki and Cai (2011, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-9469.2011.00730.x) sharpen probabilities-of-causation bounds with covariates and study conditional-monotonicity identification.
Shingaki and Kuroki (2021, NeurIPS 34) identify finite joint potential-outcome probabilities with covariate information and emphasize singular-model estimation.
Shingaki and Kuroki (2023, AAAI, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v37i10.26448) identify potential-outcome-type probabilities using proxy covariates and establish regular-case plug-in asymptotic normality.
Kawakami, Shingaki, and Kuroki (2023, AAAI, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v37i10.26442) extend response-type identification to randomized studies with noncompliance and instrument/covariate information.
Shingaki and Kuroki (2024, AISTATS, PMLR 238) identify causes-of-effects quantities using covariate-mediator information.
Shingaki, Yoshida, and Kuroki (2026, AISTATS, PMLR 300) provide the exact two-proxy and IV-plus-proxy selected-data anchor, but under regular positivity and invertibility-style conditions.
Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asy038) establish proxy identification under rank conditions and address rank failure only through causal-null testing.
Zhang et al. (2023, Statistics & Probability Letters, DOI 10.1016/j.spl.2023.109836) show that a target functional may be identified and root-n estimable even when its nuisance bridge is nonunique.
Ghassami, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (arXiv:2304.04374) develop proxy partial identification without completeness, but for causal-effect means rather than selected PN/PS cycles.
Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander (2022, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2020.1832502) derive causal bounds under outcome-dependent sampling and expose nonlinear constraints induced by selection.
Krone and Kubjas (SIAM J. Matrix Analysis and Applications; arXiv:1902.02868) and Gillis and Rajkó (2023, same venue; arXiv:2206.08022) supply NMF rigidity and partial-identifiability tools.
Allman et al. (2009, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:0809.5032) prove generic latent-class identifiability, while Allman et al. (2019, Journal of Algebraic Statistics; arXiv:1710.01696) illustrate why boundary strata require separate analysis.
de Aguas et al. (2025, CLeaR/PMLR 275; arXiv:2502.10049) and Andrews–Mikusheva (2016, Econometrica; arXiv:1409.6337) provide nearby stable-bound and weak-identification inference machinery; neither treats multinomial confidence-fiber projection through a proxy-cycle atlas.
